title: Leveraging Cache Coherence to Detect and Repair False Sharing On-the-fly
problem: False sharing performance bugs do not manifest as observable correctness errors, making them difficult to detect automatically. Prior approaches suffer from high performance overhead due to shadow memory tracking, reliance on imprecise hardware events, or limited applicability and portability.
motivation: False sharing causes significant performance degradation in multithreaded applications and requires efficient detection and mitigation without high runtime overhead or complex shadow memory mechanisms.
method: The FSDetect protocol extends MESI cache coherence to track coherence miss frequency per cache block for identifying harmful false sharing instances with negligible overhead. FSLite extends FSDetect to transparently privatize falsely shared lines on-the-fly and maintains coherence through precise byte-level updates of privatized blocks at the LLC upon termination of privatization.
key_novelty: Using cache coherence protocol extensions (FSDetect and FSLite) to detect and transparently mitigate false sharing with minimal performance overhead by tracking coherence misses and dynamic privatization.
contributions: FSDetect protocol that precisely identifies all harmful false sharing instances through coherence miss frequency tracking with negligible overhead
FSLite protocol for transparent on-the-fly privatization of falsely shared lines while maintaining coherence via byte-level LLC updates
Average 1.39X performance improvement for applications suffering from false sharing with minimal chip area increase
Demonstration of reduced network stress and improved energy behavior compared to unmodified baseline
limitations: Paper does not explicitly discuss limitations; applicability to other cache coherence protocols besides MESI not addressed.
primary_theme: Cache coherence-based false sharing detection and repair
